title: Gear & Your Motorcycle
summary: Before a trip, check the bike's equipment, get familiar with the machine, use face and eye protection, and wear proper gear.
Massachusetts requires that required safety equipment, such as horn, mirror, fenders, muffler, brakes, and lights, be in good working order.
The front needs a properly aimed white headlight; the rear needs a red taillight, a stoplight, and a white plate light, and a sidecar needs a white forward light.
A bike set up for passengers must have a secure passenger seat and separate footpegs, and handlebars may not rise above the seated operator's shoulders.
Helmets are mandatory for both riders and passengers in Massachusetts and prevent brain injury about 67% of the time.
Every helmet sold in the U.S. must meet Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 218; the two main types are three-quarter and full-face.
A helmet should fit snugly, have no cracks, loose padding, frayed straps, or exposed metal, and be securely fastened whenever you ride.
A full, shatter-resistant faceshield gives the most protection; goggles protect only the eyes, and a windshield is never a substitute for either.
Tinted eye protection should not be worn at night or in other low-light conditions.
Jackets and pants should fully cover arms and legs, boots should cover the ankles, and gloves should be leather or a durable synthetic.
Do a complete pre-ride check every time: tires, fluids, lights, turn signals, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes (one at a time), and horn.
On an unfamiliar or borrowed bike, check all controls, learn the gear pattern, and ride cautiously until you know how it handles.

questions.q: Under Massachusetts law, what color light must the front of a motorcycle be fitted with?
options: Amber
White
Red
Yellow
questions.explanation: The manual requires a properly aimed white headlight on the front of the motorcycle.

questions.q: Which set of lights must the rear of a motorcycle have?
options: An amber taillight and a white stoplight
A red taillight only
A red taillight, a stoplight, and a white license plate light
A white taillight and a red license plate light
questions.explanation: The rear must carry a red tail light, a stoplight, and a white light that illuminates the plate.

questions.q: How high may motorcycle handlebars be in Massachusetts?
options: No higher than the operator's shoulders when properly seated
No higher than the top of the operator's helmet
No higher than 15 inches above the seat
There is no height limit
questions.explanation: Handlebars must not rise above the operator's shoulders when the operator is seated properly.

questions.q: If a motorcycle is equipped to carry passengers, what must it have?
options: A backrest and grab handles
A secure passenger seat and separate passenger footpegs
A sidecar or trailer hitch
A second set of mirrors
questions.explanation: A motorcycle that carries passengers needs a secure seat for them and separate footpegs.

questions.q: Who is required to wear a helmet on a motorcycle in Massachusetts?
options: Only operators under 18
Only the operator
Only passengers
Both the operator and any passenger
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law makes helmet use mandatory for motorcycle riders and passengers alike.

questions.q: According to the manual, about how often is a motorcycle helmet effective in preventing brain injury?
options: 33% of the time
50% of the time
67% of the time
90% of the time
questions.explanation: The manual cites NHTSA data that helmets prevent brain injury roughly 67 percent of the time.

questions.q: Motorcycle helmets sold in the United States must meet which standard?
options: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 218
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 108
VESC-8
SAE J1100
questions.explanation: FMVSS No. 218 sets the minimum protection level that all helmets sold in the U.S. must provide.

questions.q: What are the two main types of motorcycle helmets described in the manual?
options: Half-shell and modular
Three-quarter and full-face
Open-face and half-shell
Motocross and touring
questions.explanation: The manual names three-quarter and full-face helmets as the two types, each offering a different level of coverage.

questions.q: Before buying a used helmet, what should you first make sure of?
options: That it is less than two years old
That it has a tinted visor
That it has never been worn by a passenger
That its manufacturer or distributor will re-inspect it for damage
questions.explanation: Helmet damage is not always visible, so the manual advises confirming the maker or distributor will re-inspect a used helmet.

questions.q: Which type of eye and face protection does the manual recommend for the best protection?
options: A full, shatter-resistant faceshield
A tall windshield
Shatter-resistant sunglasses
Prescription eyeglasses
questions.explanation: The manual recommends a full faceshield to protect the eyes and face from the elements and road hazards.

questions.q: Which statement about windshields is correct according to the manual?
options: A windshield replaces the need for goggles
A windshield is acceptable eye protection during the day only
A windshield is not a substitute for a faceshield or goggles
A windshield gives more protection than a faceshield
questions.explanation: The manual states plainly that a windshield cannot stand in for a faceshield or goggles.

questions.q: When should tinted eye protection NOT be worn?
options: In bright sunlight
At night or whenever little light is available
On the highway
When it is raining in daylight
questions.explanation: Tinted protection reduces vision, so the manual says not to use it at night or in other low-light conditions.

questions.q: Which is a requirement for effective eye and faceshield protection?
options: It must be tinted
It must seal tightly so no air passes through
It must be free of scratches and give a clear view to either side
It must be attached to the windshield
questions.explanation: Effective protection must be scratch-free and provide clear side vision; it should also let air through to reduce fogging.

questions.q: According to the manual, what should riding boots or shoes be like?
options: High enough to cover the ankles, with hard, durable, slip-resistant soles
Low-cut for easier shifting
Soft-soled with tall heels for better reach
Laced loosely with the laces left outside
questions.explanation: Footwear should cover and support the ankles, have tough slip-resistant soles, short heels, and tucked-in laces.

questions.q: During a pre-ride check, how should you test the brakes?
options: Apply both brakes together while rolling downhill
Try the front and rear brakes one at a time and make sure each feels firm and holds the motorcycle
Pump the rear brake only until it feels firm
Brakes only need to be checked at the annual inspection
questions.explanation: The checklist says to test each brake separately and confirm it is firm and holds the bike when fully applied.

questions.q: You are about to ride a borrowed motorcycle. What does the manual advise?
options: Skip the safety checks since the owner maintains it
Ride at normal speed to learn its handling quickly
Check the controls, learn the gear pattern, and ride very cautiously until familiar with it
Only check the fuel level
questions.explanation: On an unfamiliar bike you should do all your usual checks, learn the controls and shift pattern, and ride carefully until you know how it handles.
